newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan protests to go on despite day of violence.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan protests to go on despite day of violence.

text.p: Kenyan opposition groups vowed to resume protests demanding constitutional reforms despite the deaths of several people in clashes with police on Monday, the country's worst day of political violence for seven years.
The National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC), made up of opposition parties, human rights groups and other bodies, late on Monday ordered new demonstrations to put pressure on the government.
The NCEC called for three days of national mourning from Wednesday to Friday "for the gallant sons and daughters who were killed by the government during the Saba Saba commemoration".
Rallies in Nairobi and several towns and cities across the country were called on Monday to commemorate the killings of 20 people on July 7, known as Saba Saba in Kiswahili, 1990, at a Nairobi rally.

The NCEC said Kenyans on Wednesday would "demonstrate their displeasure" with the government hosting a summit on Sudan's civil war under the six-nation Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) in Nairobi during the mourning period.
"Our position and demand of the IGAD meeting is no reforms, no IGAD meeting," the NCEC said in a statement. Police said they would block any demonstrators who failed to apply for a permit.
"The campaign for civil disobedience must continue if no tangible actions are seen towards reforms. Towns will be closed down many times in the future," said Koigi wa Wamwere, a leading dissident.

Joseph Kamotho, secretary-general of President Daniel arap Moi's ruling Kenya African National Union party, condemned Monday's violence as part of a plot to hijack democracy, block the impending general election and seize power by force.

He condemned the violence and "defiance of authority" and said the reform programme would start with the elections followed by steps to review the constitution. The opposition says reforms must be made before the election to serve any purpose.
The NCEC says the law requiring a permit for demonstrations is itself unconstitutional and therefore is null and void.
Moi, 73, is almost certain to win another five-year term from this year's presidential and parliamentary elections, for which no dates have been set, because the opposition is split.

Police and paramilitary officers stormed Nairobi's main Anglican cathedral All Saints, fired teargas inside and beat people including Muturi Kigano, head of the unregistered Safina party, and opposition parliamentarians Kamau Icharia and Njoka Mutahi.
But David Gitari, the archbishop of Kenya, condemned the police invasion and demanded it be respected as a sanctuary.

The Rev. Timothy Njoya, the moderator of the Presbyterian Church of East Africa and an organiser of the demonstrations, was severely beaten near the cathedral by six police wielding wooden pick-axe handles. His assistant was also bady hurt.
Police seemed to single out rally organisers for especially harsh beatings but they also rained blows from batons and clubs on everyone they caught, including people who did not resist.
Police said Red Cross workers found a boy bleeding from his mouth and ears in Nairobi's Uhuru park but he died en route to hospital. They said they would investigate all Monday's deaths.
Witnesses told Reuters David Mutugi, 17, was shot in the chest and killed by police in Thika, 20 miles (30 km) northeast of Nairobi, when police and prison guards charged a crowd.

In addition, police spokesman Assistant Commissioner Peter Kimanthi said four men were killed in Nyahururu town and a man was shot dead by a gunman in a private car and the boy died of his wounds in Nairobi.
Kimanthi said two men were killed in a stampede when 3,000 people heading for the prison in Nyahururu, 100 km (60 miles) west of Nairobi, were dispersed by police and prison officers.
Two more men were shot by police in Nyahururu when a mob attempted to storm a bank and broke windows, he added.
Kenyan newspaper journalists however said they had witness reports that all four men in Nyahururu were shot by police.
